dedupe_keys.name: occupancy simulator lbnl agent based stochastic occupant schedules for commercial buildings

description: The Occupancy Simulator is a web app from Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory that simulates occupant movement in a building with a Markov-chain model. From high-level inputs on occupants, spaces and events it generates occupant schedules for each space that capture the diversity and randomness of occupant activity, and the schedules can be downloaded for building energy simulation. The algorithms are described by Chen, Hong and Luo (2017) and evaluated by Luo and colleagues (2017); development was sponsored by the U.S. Department of Energy and belongs to IEA EBC Annex 66 on occupant behaviour. Coverage: commercial buildings. Access: free use in the browser, with a PDF tutorial. Licence: not stated. Caveats: the page lists limits: no residential, hotel or school types, no walking time between spaces, holidays set per building, not per person, presence independent of indoor conditions, and a meeting room model based on one room's calendar. Simulation uses: realistic occupancy schedules for building energy, ventilation and space use studies. Related records: obFMU, EnergyPlus and the ASHRAE global occupant behaviour database.
